es: Distinguir en una noticia los hechos verificables, las afirmaciones sin prueba y las opiniones, y reconocer sus señales.

teaching.en: The report states that the library opened in 1998, and anyone can verify the date.
teaching.es: El informe afirma que la biblioteca abrió en 1998, y cualquiera puede comprobar la fecha.
teaching.explanationEs: Un hecho se puede comprobar en un registro; verify = comprobar.
segments: The report states that the library opened in
1998, and anyone can verify the date.
teaching.audioText: The report states that the library opened in 1998, and anyone can verify the date.

teaching.en: The website claims that the new app doubles your reading speed, but it offers no evidence.
teaching.es: La web afirma que la nueva app duplica tu velocidad de lectura, pero no ofrece pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Claims anuncia algo que todavía necesita prueba; evidence es incontable: no lleva -s.
segments: The website claims that the new app doubles
your reading speed, but it offers no evidence.
teaching.audioText: The website claims that the new app doubles your reading speed, but it offers no evidence.

teaching.en: In my opinion, the new stadium looks far better than the old one.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, el nuevo estadio se ve mucho mejor que el viejo.
teaching.explanationEs: Un juicio personal se marca con in my opinion; «según yo» no existe en inglés.
segments: In my opinion, the new stadium looks
far better than the old one.
teaching.audioText: In my opinion, the new stadium looks far better than the old one.

teaching.en: The video allegedly shows the mayor leaving the meeting early.
teaching.es: El vídeo supuestamente muestra a la alcaldesa saliendo pronto de la reunión.
teaching.explanationEs: Allegedly avisa de que nadie lo ha demostrado todavía.
segments: The video allegedly shows the
mayor leaving the meeting early.
teaching.audioText: The video allegedly shows the mayor leaving the meeting early.

teaching.en: According to the figures, forty per cent of students sleep less than seven hours.
teaching.es: Según las cifras, el cuarenta por ciento de los estudiantes duerme menos de siete horas.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + fuente introduce un dato que se puede comprobar; figures = cifras.
segments: According to the figures, forty per cent
of students sleep less than seven hours.
teaching.audioText: According to the figures, forty per cent of students sleep less than seven hours.

teaching.en: Before you share a statement online, ask who the source is.
teaching.es: Antes de compartir una declaración en internet, pregunta quién es la fuente.
teaching.explanationEs: Toda declaración debería tener una fuente que puedas identificar.
segments: Before you share a statement online,
ask who the source is.
teaching.audioText: Before you share a statement online, ask who the source is.

prompt.es: Elige el enunciado que es un hecho verificable.

choices.text: The library is the most beautiful building in town.
The library allegedly hides a secret room.
The library opened in 1998, according to the town's records.

feedback.es: Un hecho verificable se apoya en un registro que se puede consultar; los otros son un juicio personal y un rumor.

hint.es: Busca el que cita un registro que cualquiera puede consultar.

prompt.es: Completa: «La publicación supuestamente muestra a una cantante famosa comprando una casa.»

answer.text: allegedly

feedback.es: Allegedly avisa de que lo que muestra la publicación nadie lo ha probado aún.

origin.text: The post ___ shows a famous singer buying a house.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Según las cifras, la mayoría de los estudiantes va andando al colegio.»

answer.text: According to the figures most students walk to school
accepted: According to the figures most students walk to school
Most students walk to school according to the figures

feedback.es: According to the figures abre la frase y presenta un dato que se puede comprobar.

hint.es: La fuente va delante: According to the figures…

prompt.es: ¿Qué enunciado es una opinión y no un hecho?

The museum opened in 1985.
The museum has two floors.

feedback.es: «The most boring» es un juicio personal; la fecha y el número de plantas se pueden comprobar.

She sees it as a claim with no evidence.
She sees it as her own opinion.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada señal con el tipo de enunciado que anuncia.

feedback.es: Cada señal anuncia un tipo distinto: fuente comprobable, afirmación sin probar o juicio personal.

choices.text: The new bus lane opened in March.
This is the best decision in years.
The lane allegedly cut journeys by half.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué es un hecho lo que dice la profesora.

choices.text: She shows data that anyone can check.
She gives her personal view of the experiment.
She repeats a rumour from a friend.

origin.text: The article does not give any ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Antes de compartirlo, comprueba quién es la fuente.»

answer.text: Before you share it check who the source is
accepted: Before you share it check who the source is
Check who the source is before you share it

feedback.es: La orden empieza con la cláusula de tiempo y termina con la pregunta indirecta «who the source is».

In my opinion, this app is too difficult.
By my opinion, this app is too difficult.

feedback.es: Para tu parecer se usa in my opinion; «according to me» y «by my opinion» son calcos del español.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase que presente la noticia como afirmación sin prueba.

answer.text: The website claims that the drink makes you clever, but it shows no evidence.
accepted: The website claims that the drink makes you clever, but it shows no evidence.
The website allegedly proves that the drink makes you clever, but it offers no evidence.
The site claims that the drink makes you clever, but it gives no proof.

feedback.es: Una afirmación sin prueba combina claims o allegedly con la falta de evidence.

origin.text: La web dice que su bebida te hace más listo, pero no muestra ninguna prueba.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase sobre las pruebas suena natural?

choices.text: The article gives a lot of evidences.
The article gives many evidences.
The article gives a lot of evidence.

feedback.es: Evidence es incontable, por eso se dice a lot of evidence y nunca evidences.

es: Distinguir causa, correlación y posibilidad con el verbo adecuado (causes, is linked to, may account for) y corregir causas exageradas.

teaching.en: Heavy rain causes the river to flood, so rain is the cause of the damage.
teaching.es: La lluvia fuerte hace que el río se desborde, así que la lluvia es la causa del daño.
teaching.explanationEs: Causes, leads to y results in afirman una causa ya comprobada.
segments: Heavy rain causes the river to flood, so
rain is the cause of the damage.
teaching.audioText: Heavy rain causes the river to flood, so rain is the cause of the damage.

teaching.en: Too little sleep leads to poor results, and several studies confirm the trend.
teaching.es: Dormir poco provoca malos resultados, y varios estudios confirman la tendencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Leads to + sustantivo: A provoca B; trend = tendencia que se repite.
segments: Too little sleep leads to poor results,
and several studies confirm the trend.
teaching.audioText: Too little sleep leads to poor results, and several studies confirm the trend.

teaching.en: Reading for pleasure is linked to higher exam marks, but a link is not proof.
teaching.es: Leer por placer se relaciona con mejores notas de examen, pero una relación no es una prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Is linked to describe dos cosas que van juntas, sin decir cuál provoca cuál.
segments: Reading for pleasure is linked to higher exam
marks, but a link is not proof.
teaching.audioText: Reading for pleasure is linked to higher exam marks, but a link is not proof.

teaching.en: There is a strong correlation between ice cream sales and swimming accidents.
teaching.es: Hay una fuerte correlación entre las ventas de helados y los accidentes al nadar.
teaching.explanationEs: Correlation between X and Y: con between … and, no con of.
segments: There is a strong correlation between
ice cream sales and swimming accidents.
teaching.audioText: There is a strong correlation between ice cream sales and swimming accidents.

teaching.en: Hot weather may account for both figures; ice cream is not necessarily the cause.
teaching.es: El calor puede explicar ambas cifras; el helado no es necesariamente la causa.
teaching.explanationEs: May account for expresa una explicación posible; not necessarily = no tiene por qué.
segments: Hot weather may account for both figures;
ice cream is not necessarily the cause.
teaching.audioText: Hot weather may account for both figures; ice cream is not necessarily the cause.

teaching.en: It could be a coincidence that there was a rise in both during the same summer.
teaching.es: Podría ser una casualidad que hubiera un aumento en ambos durante el mismo verano.
teaching.explanationEs: Could/may/might + be marcan duda; coincidence = casualidad; rise = aumento.
segments: It could be a coincidence that there was
a rise in both during the same summer.
teaching.audioText: It could be a coincidence that there was a rise in both during the same summer.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe una relación sin afirmar causa.

choices.text: Owning a dog is linked to lower stress in this survey.
Owning a dog causes lower stress in every home.
Owning a dog leads to lower stress, and that is proved.

feedback.es: Is linked to describe una relación observada en una encuesta; causes y leads to afirman una causa.

hint.es: Busca el verbo que solo dice que dos cosas van juntas.

prompt.es: Completa: «El retraso puede explicar las ventas bajas.»

answer.text: may

feedback.es: Un modal de posibilidad seguido de account for presenta una explicación posible, no segura.

hint.es: Necesitas un modal que exprese posibilidad.

origin.text: The delay ___ account for the low sales.

feedback.es: La correlación se construye con between … and, y aquí no dice que uno cause al otro.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que afirma una causa probada.

choices.text: Heavy traffic is linked to air pollution in this city.
Heavy traffic causes air pollution, and tests confirm it.
Heavy traffic may account for some of the air pollution.

feedback.es: Causes junto con la confirmación de las pruebas expresa una causa; las otras dos son relación y posibilidad.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hubo un aumento en ambos casos, pero podría ser una casualidad.»

answer.text: coincidence

feedback.es: Could be a coincidence reconoce que dos aumentos pueden coincidir por azar.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concluye el locutor.

choices.text: Umbrellas clearly cause colds.
Colds make people buy umbrellas.
Rain may explain both, so there is no direct cause.

feedback.es: El locutor propone que la lluvia explique ambos aumentos, así que no hay causa directa entre ellos.

prompt.es: Completa: causa comprobada en la primera frase, relación en la segunda.

answer.text: leads | linked

feedback.es: La primera frase afirma una causa con leads to; la segunda solo vincula dos datos con linked to.

sentences: Too much sugar ___ to health problems, and studies confirm it.

prompt.es: Suaviza esta causa exagerada con una relación y un modal de duda.

accepted: Video games may be linked to lower marks in teenagers.
Video games might be associated with bad marks in teenagers.
There may be a correlation between video games and bad marks in teens.

choices.text: Cold weather may be linked to more colds.
Cold weather always causes colds.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo presenta la locutora el papel de las luces.

choices.text: The lights are the proved cause of the fall.
The lights are possibly one factor among several.
The lights have no link with the fall at all.

feedback.es: La locutora dice que las luces podrían explicar parte de la bajada y que otros factores también importan.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El aumento puede explicar ambas tendencias.»

answer.text: The rise may account for both trends

feedback.es: May account for presenta el aumento como explicación posible de las dos tendencias.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con lo que afirma.

feedback.es: Leads to afirma causa, is linked to solo relaciona y might account for deja una explicación posible.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta sobre una correlación.

choices.text: There is a strong correlation of age and salary.
There is a strong correlation among age to salary.
There is a strong correlation between age and salary.

feedback.es: Correlation se combina con between … and; of y among … to no funcionan.

es: Reconocer en publicaciones breves el falso dilema, la generalización apresurada, el ataque personal y el sesgo, y nombrar la debilidad con una razón.

teaching.en: Either we ban phones completely or students will never learn: this fallacy is a false dilemma.
teaching.es: O prohibimos los móviles por completo o los estudiantes nunca aprenderán: esta falacia es un falso dilema.
teaching.explanationEs: Un falso dilema presenta solo dos opciones cuando hay más; fallacy = falacia.
segments: Either we ban phones completely or students will
never learn: this fallacy is a false dilemma.
teaching.audioText: Either we ban phones completely or students will never learn: this fallacy is a false dilemma.

teaching.en: My cousin met two rude tourists, so all tourists are rude: that is a hasty generalisation.
teaching.es: Mi primo conoció a dos turistas maleducados, así que todos los turistas son maleducados: es una generalización apresurada.
teaching.explanationEs: Generalización apresurada: pocos casos se convierten en una regla para todos.
segments: My cousin met two rude tourists, so all
tourists are rude: that is a hasty generalisation.
teaching.audioText: My cousin met two rude tourists, so all tourists are rude: that is a hasty generalisation.

teaching.en: A sample of two people is far too small to prove anything.
teaching.es: Una muestra de dos personas es demasiado pequeña para probar nada.
teaching.explanationEs: Sample = muestra; too small to + verbo: demasiado pequeña para…
segments: A sample of two people is
far too small to prove anything.
teaching.audioText: A sample of two people is far too small to prove anything.

teaching.en: His reply was an attack on her age, not an answer to her argument.
teaching.es: Su respuesta fue un ataque a su edad, no una respuesta a su argumento.
teaching.explanationEs: Ataque personal: se ataca a quien habla, no a lo que dice.
segments: His reply was an attack on her
age, not an answer to her argument.
teaching.audioText: His reply was an attack on her age, not an answer to her argument.

teaching.en: The survey asked only the club's fans, so the result shows a clear bias.
teaching.es: La encuesta preguntó solo a los aficionados del club, así que el resultado muestra un claro sesgo.
teaching.explanationEs: Bias: la fuente o la muestra favorece una conclusión.
segments: The survey asked only the club's fans,
so the result shows a clear bias.
teaching.audioText: The survey asked only the club's fans, so the result shows a clear bias.

teaching.en: Never assume that a popular post is a true one; look for its weakness first.
teaching.es: Nunca des por hecho que una publicación popular es verdadera; busca antes su punto débil.
teaching.explanationEs: Assume = dar por hecho; weakness = punto débil de un argumento.
segments: Never assume that a popular post is a
true one; look for its weakness first.
teaching.audioText: Never assume that a popular post is a true one; look for its weakness first.

origin.text: A ___ of two people is too small to prove anything.

es: Escribir una crítica matizada de una publicación: dos críticas justificadas, una relación con modal de duda y una alternativa razonable.

teaching.en: The post seems to overlook the fact that the sample was tiny.
teaching.es: La publicación parece pasar por alto que la muestra era diminuta.
teaching.explanationEs: Seems to + verbo suaviza la crítica: parece que…; overlook = pasar por alto.
segments: The post seems to overlook the
fact that the sample was tiny.
teaching.audioText: The post seems to overlook the fact that the sample was tiny.

teaching.en: Arguably, the writer's strongest point is also the least supported one.
teaching.es: Se podría argumentar que el punto más fuerte del autor es también el menos respaldado.
teaching.explanationEs: Arguably abre un juicio cauteloso que invita a discutir.
segments: Arguably, the writer's strongest point is
also the least supported one.
teaching.audioText: Arguably, the writer's strongest point is also the least supported one.

teaching.en: To some extent the claim is fair, but it is likely to be exaggerated.
teaching.es: Hasta cierto punto la afirmación es justa, pero es probable que esté exagerada.
teaching.explanationEs: To some extent concede una parte; is likely to + verbo = es probable que…
segments: To some extent the claim is fair,
but it is likely to be exaggerated.
teaching.audioText: To some extent the claim is fair, but it is likely to be exaggerated.

teaching.en: Rather than blaming the students, a balanced post would ask why they are tired.

segments: Rather than blaming the students, a balanced

teaching.audioText: Rather than blaming the students, a balanced post would ask why they are tired.

teaching.explanationEs: Una relación se matiza con likely o un modal de duda, como en la clase anterior.
segments: The rise in complaints is likely to be linked
to the new rules, although other factors may matter.
teaching.audioText: The rise in complaints is likely to be linked to the new rules, although other factors may matter.

prompt.es: Escribe una crítica (130–250 palabras): dos críticas, relación con duda y alternativa.

answer.text: I read the blog post about mobile phones and marks, and I think it has two important weaknesses. First, it seems to rely on a very small sample: the writer asked only five friends, so the result cannot speak for the whole school. Arguably, this is the main weakness, because five friends are not enough to prove anything. Second, the post is one-sided. It says the solution is to ban phones, but that is a false dilemma, because there are many other options. To some extent, the writer is right: the fall in marks may be linked to phones, and phones are likely to distract some students. However, a link is not proof, and other factors, such as stress or sleep, may account for the trend. A more balanced alternative would be to survey every class and then agree some simple rules, rather than ban everything. In my opinion, that would be fairer and more reasonable for everybody.

A more balanced alternative would be to survey every class and then agree some simple rules, rather than ban everything. In my opinion, that would be fairer and more reasonable for everybody.

Hello, I want to give my view of the post about phones. It seems to ignore a basic problem: the sample is tiny, because the writer asked only five friends. Arguably, that is enough to make the conclusion weak. The post also offers only two choices, ban phones or lose the marks, and that is a false dilemma. To some extent the writer has a point, because the drop in marks is likely to be linked to phones, but it could also be a coincidence, and other factors may account for it. A reasonable alternative would be to survey every class, rather than five friends, and to agree simple rules together. In my opinion, a more balanced post would be clearer and more useful.

prompt.es: Escribe una verificación de 130–250 palabras con tres afirmaciones y un veredicto.

answer.text: I checked the viral story about the school closing, and I rate it as unproven. First, the post says the council has cut the budget in half, but it comes from an account with no name and gives no source, so we cannot confirm it. Second, the photo of the empty building is real, but it is misleading, because it was taken during last year's summer holidays, out of context. Third, the headline says most families have left, but it is based on a survey of only ten families, so it is a hasty generalisation. There is no evidence that the school will close, and the original source is missing. To find out more, we need the council's official report and the real number of students. Based on the evidence available, the story is likely to be false, although we may be wrong if new figures appear. In conclusion, readers should not share it until a reliable source confirms it.
accepted: I checked the viral story about the school closing, and I rate it as unproven. First, the post says the council has cut the budget in half, but it comes from an account with no name and gives no source, so we cannot confirm it. Second, the photo of the empty building is real, but it is misleading, because it was taken during last year's summer holidays, out of context. Third, the headline says most families have left, but it is based on a survey of only ten families, so it is a hasty generalisation. There is no evidence that the school will close, and the original source is missing. To find out more, we need the council's official report and the real number of students. Based on the evidence available, the story is likely to be false, although we may be wrong if new figures appear. In conclusion, readers should not share it until a reliable source confirms it.

My verdict on the viral story is that it is unproven. The first claim, that the council has cut the budget in half, has no source, so we cannot confirm it. The second claim uses a real photo of the empty building, but it is misleading, because the photo shows the summer holidays and not a closed school. The third claim, that most families have left, comes from a survey of only ten families, which is too small a sample. There is no evidence that the school will close. We still need the original source and the official figures from the council. Based on the evidence available, the story is likely to be false, but it may change if new evidence appears. In conclusion, please do not share it yet.
